source_basis.reclaim_text: LOCAL_RECLAIM: price closes on S5 back through a causally known fast pivot/reclaim level in parent direction d.
causal_implications: "back through" can mean an actual completed-S5 edge crossing rather than merely being beyond the level
a reclaim pivot may be an event-owned state object that is consumed by a successful reclaim/reacceleration attempt rather than freely reusable forever

frozen_semantics: 13E original-event lifetime constraint retained as causal diagnostic only
13F S15 reclaim pivot ownership search result; no 13F profile promoted
completed S5 reclaim and later completed-S5 reacceleration

profiles.semantics: 13F strict post-original-pullback pivot, unlimited reuse, current completed S5 close only must be beyond level.
13F inherited-first profile, unlimited reuse, current completed S5 close beyond level.
post-original-pullback pivot; completed S5 reclaim requires previous completed S5 close on the adverse side/equal and current close on parent side.
first attempt may inherit an already-causal pivot, later attempts require post-original-pullback pivot; every reclaim requires a true completed-S5 edge crossing.

strict post-original-pullback provenance; after a successful ENTRY_ELIGIBLE signal the exact reclaim pivot identity used by that attempt is consumed and cannot be reused until a different causal pivot identity is current.

first attempt may inherit any already-causal pivot; after signal the pivot identity used by the successful attempt is consumed; later pivot must be post-original-pullback and different from the consumed identity.
combine inherited-first provenance, actual completed-S5 edge crossing, and successful-attempt pivot consumption.

selection_rule: No threshold tuning. Preserve exact 13F strict and inherited-first controls. Prefer a source-compatible crossing/consumption rule only if it materially narrows trade-count and raw-win gaps while preserving the near-historical economic scale; exact count alone is insufficient.
